name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; England rising from low
summary: US flu admissions at a seasonal high not seen since 2010-11; England's flu activity above baseline but low impact
state: US hospitals logged 6,100 flu admissions in the week to 24 Oct, the highest rate for that week since 2010-11, and the CDC forecast a further rise to mid-November (Nature World News, 4 Nov). UKHSA reported on 5 Nov that flu positivity in England rose to 7.6% in the week to 1 Nov, still in the low-impact range; its next weekly report was not yet out on 12 Nov. An unusually early US season meets Watch; no health systems are reported as strained.
for_you: Older people, young children, pregnant women and those with long-term conditions are most exposed to severe flu. The NHS sets out who is eligible for a free flu vaccine and how to book one.
rubric_hit: Unusually early flu season: US week-42 admission rate highest since 2010-11; no system strain, so not Alert

sources.title: Nature World News — CDC forecasts flu hospitalizations will likely keep climbing through mid-November
UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026 (week 45)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
